newsitem.title: IRAQ: ICRC officials discuss missing Kuwaitis with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: ICRC officials discuss missing Kuwaitis with Iraq.

text.p: A senior official of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is in Baghdad to discuss the issue of Kuwaitis reported missing during Iraq's seven month occupation of Kuwait, an ICRC official said on Sunday.

Manuel Bessler, head of the ICRC office in Baghdad, said executive council member and director of operations Jean de Courten had met Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz on Sunday and discussed the fate of some 600 Kuwaitis and others missing since the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
"We have discussed with Aziz the subject of missing Kuwaitis," Bessler said after their meeting with the Iraqi deputy premier.

Kuwait and its ally the United States say a full accounting for more than 600 Kuwaitis and others is one of the conditions Iraq must meet before economic sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion can be lifted.
"We exchanged points of view and we hope that these dicussions would lead to concrete results in this issue," the ICRC official said.
Iraq has repeatedly denied holding any Kuwaitis in its prisons, saying it would do it no good keeping them in jail since their detention would prolong sanctions.
Bessler said de Courten's visit to Iraq was also to discuss prisoners held since the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran War.
"The ICRC continues its efforts to find a solution to this problem with all parties concerned," he added.
The official Iraqi News Agency, reporting the meeting, said Aziz had urged the ICRC to press Tehran to release Iraqi prisoners of war (POWs).
Iraq says Iran is still holding 18,275 Iraqi POWs, 8,718 of them registered by the ICRC. Information on the others was gathered from letters they sent through the ICRC to relatives in Iraq.
Baghdad says it freed 39,044 Iranian POWs in a large-scale exchange of prisoners in 1990 and denies Iranian claims that it still has more on its territory.
The POW issue is among the thorniest blocking the normalisation of ties. Iranian and Iraqi officials have held several meetings to solve the problem but to no avail.
